# Configuration reference

Every tunable of the backend is an environment variable with the prefix `OPENDEX_` (a `.env` file next to where the backend starts is read too). Nothing is hard-coded at call sites. Values are validated at start-up; an invalid value stops the backend with a message instead of running half-configured.

78 settings, generated from [`backend/app/config.py`](../backend/app/config.py) — the comment above each setting there is the description below.


## ADB / scrcpy

| Variable | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `OPENDEX_ADB_PATH` | `str` | `adb` | The adb executable: a name found on PATH, or a full path. |
| `OPENDEX_ADB_SERIAL` | `str \| None` | *(unset)* | The default device serial for adb commands that name none (a USB serial or `host:port`); unset: adb's own default. |
| `OPENDEX_SCRCPY_CLIENT_VERSION` | `str` | `4.1` | The scrcpy protocol version the backend speaks; it selects vendor/scrcpy-server-v<version>[-opendex]. |
| `OPENDEX_SCRCPY_SERVER_FLAVOR` | `Literal['auto', 'upstream', 'opendex']` | `auto` | Which scrcpy-server binary is pushed. "opendex": the patched build of the same version (backend/scrcpy — leading-edge resize debouncer, OPENDEX_RESIZE, bitrate on reset), "upstream": Genymobile's release, "auto": the patched build when vendor/ has it, else upstream. Resolved to "upstream" or "opendex" at load. What a running server can do is learned from its own announcement, never from this setting, so the wrong binary under either name only means today's behaviour. Rollback: "upstream". |
| `OPENDEX_SCRCPY_SERVER_PATH` | `Path \| None` | *(unset)* | None: derived from the flavor (vendor/scrcpy-server-v<version>[-opendex]). An explicit path is used as given. |
| `OPENDEX_SCRCPY_RESIZE_MIN_INTERVAL_MS` | `int` | `300` | Patched server only: least time between two flex display resizes (its leading-edge debouncer). |
| `OPENDEX_SCRCPY_DEVICE_SERVER_PATH` | `str` | `/data/local/tmp/opendex-scrcpy-server.jar` | Where the server jar is pushed on the phone. |

## HTTP

| Variable | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `OPENDEX_HTTP_HOST` | `str` | `127.0.0.1` | The address the API listens on. Anything but loopback is refused unless ALLOW_REMOTE is true and API_TOKEN is set. |
| `OPENDEX_HTTP_PORT` | `int` | `8710` | The port of the API (the bundled UI and the dev proxy expect 8710). |
| `OPENDEX_LOG_LEVEL` | `str` | `INFO` | Log level of the backend: DEBUG, INFO, WARNING or ERROR (also changeable at run time: POST /diagnostics/log-level). The log file gets INFO and above unless this is DEBUG or a trace is on. |
| `OPENDEX_CORS_ORIGINS` | `list[str]` | *(12 entries)* | http://localhost:5173 = Vite dev server (`npm run dev` / `npm run tauri dev`'s beforeDevCommand). The packaged Tauri app (`opendex.exe`, the backend sidecar build) is a DIFFERENT origin at runtime — WebView2 on Windows serves Tauri's bundled frontend from https://tauri.localhost, never localhost:5173 — so without it here every fetch() from the packaged exe to this API (QR generation included — usually the FIRST request the UI makes, hence the earliest visible symptom) was silently blocked by this exact allowlist. tauri://localhost included too as a defensive alias for other platforms' custom-protocol origin naming. |

## Authentication

| Variable | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `OPENDEX_API_TOKEN` | `str \| None` | *(unset)* | The bearer token every /api and /ws call must present. Empty: the per-user file below is used (created 0600 on first start). Set it explicitly when the API must be reachable from another machine. |
| `OPENDEX_API_TOKEN_FILE` | `Path` | `~/.opendex/api-token` | The per-user token file, used when API_TOKEN is empty. |
| `OPENDEX_DAEMON_TOKEN_FILE` | `Path` | `~/.opendex/daemon-token` | The secret the on-device daemon is started with and the backend answers its challenge with (device/daemon_auth.py). A different file from the API token on purpose: that one reaches the browser UI, this one never leaves the backend. |
| `OPENDEX_DAEMON_SHELL` | `bool` | `true` | Device shell commands go to the daemon first (device/adb.py). False is the way back: every command runs on adb, as before — for comparing the two paths on a device, or if a phone's daemon misbehaves. The daemon itself (media, volume, tasks, …) is unaffected. |
| `OPENDEX_ALLOW_REMOTE` | `bool` | `false` | Listening beyond loopback is refused unless this is true AND API_TOKEN is set explicitly. |
| `OPENDEX_TOKEN_BOOTSTRAP` | `bool` | `false` | GET /api/auth/bootstrap hands the token to a browser page from one of the app's own origins. Only for the nginx/Docker deployment, where nothing else can give the page the token; the desktop build leaves it off. |
| `OPENDEX_MAX_BODY_BYTES` | `int` | `2000000` | Largest request body a route may receive (settings, layouts and client-log batches are a few KB). |
| `OPENDEX_WS_MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES` | `int` | `8000000` | Largest single WebSocket message uvicorn accepts (/ws/input, /ws/events — /ws/video and /ws/audio* only ever send). The one legitimately large payload is a clipboard paste (arbitrary, uncapped text); this stays a small fraction of uvicorn's 16 MB default, which existed only to let a client make the backend allocate. |
| `OPENDEX_API_DOCS` | `bool` | `false` | Interactive API docs (/docs, /openapi.json) — a development aid, off in the product. |
| `OPENDEX_ALLOWED_HOSTS` | `list[str]` | `["127.0.0.1", "::1", "localhost"]` | Host names the API answers to (app/api/origin_guard.py): anything else is a DNS-rebinding attempt. Loopback and every *.localhost name are always accepted; add a LAN name here only together with real authentication. |

## File system

| Variable | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `OPENDEX_FS_ENABLED` | `bool` | `true` | False turns the file manager off: its routes answer 404. |
| `OPENDEX_FS_PC_ACCESS` | `Literal['folders', 'home', 'all']` | `folders` | How much of THIS PC the file manager may touch: "folders" (Desktop/Documents/Downloads/Pictures/Music/Videos and folders the user adds), "home" (the whole user profile) or "all" (every drive). OpenDeX's own data folder and the usual credential stores stay closed in every mode (fs/roots.py). |
| `OPENDEX_FS_EXTRA_ROOTS` | `list[Path]` | `[]` | Extra PC folders the file manager may browse, in addition to its defaults. |
| `OPENDEX_FS_ADB_HOST` | `str` | `127.0.0.1` | Where adb's server listens: the file transfers open their own streams on it (fs/adb_sync.py). |
| `OPENDEX_FS_ADB_PORT` | `int` | `5037` | the adb server's port |
| `OPENDEX_FS_TRANSFER_WORKERS` | `int` | `3` | files in flight per job |
| `OPENDEX_FS_MAX_JOBS` | `int` | `2` | jobs running at once; the rest wait, queued |
| `OPENDEX_FS_CACHE_DIR` | `Path` | `~/.opendex/cache/fs` | the OLD on-disk preview cache: only ever cleaned up |
| `OPENDEX_FS_CACHE_MB` | `int` | `256` | RAM kept for previewed phone files (never written to the disk) |
| `OPENDEX_FS_THUMB_CACHE_MB` | `int` | `48` | RAM kept for thumbnails |
| `OPENDEX_FS_PREVIEW_MAX_MB` | `int` | `96` | a bigger phone file is copied, not previewed (also capped by FS_CACHE_MB) |
| `OPENDEX_FS_TRASH_DAYS` | `int` | `30` | the phone's Recycle Bin keeps items this long (0: for ever) |
| `OPENDEX_FS_SHELL_TOKEN_FILE` | `Path` | `~/.opendex/shell-token` | Only the Tauri shell can read this file: it proves a drag-and-drop / file-picker grant came from native UI. |

## Video defaults

| Variable | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `OPENDEX_DEFAULT_MAX_FPS` | `int` | `60` | Frame-rate cap of a new window's stream. |
| `OPENDEX_DEFAULT_VIDEO_BIT_RATE` | `int` | `8000000` | Video bit rate in bit/s. Raised (never lowered) for large windows — see MIN_BITS_PER_PIXEL_PER_FRAME. |
| `OPENDEX_DEFAULT_MAX_SIZE` | `int` | `1280` | The longest side, in pixels, of a window's video. |
| `OPENDEX_DEFAULT_VIDEO_CODEC` | `str` | `auto` | "auto", "h264", "h265" or "av1" — the project setting `video_codec` overrides it. |
| `OPENDEX_MIN_BITS_PER_PIXEL_PER_FRAME` | `float` | `0.04` | video_bit_rate was a single, resolution-agnostic project setting: opening a small windowed panel and later growing it (dynamic bucket growth, or dynamic_fit continuously enlarging) never re-examined it, so the SAME bitrate budget that looked fine at a small size kept being reused at a much larger one — visible blocking/softness ("kalite düşüyor"), worst on screen content (sharp text/UI edges compress far worse than camera video). This is a FLOOR, not a fixed value: max(configured, w*h*fps*this) — window_manager._resolution_aware_bitrate() — so it only ever RAISES an under-provisioned bitrate for a large target, never lowers what the user explicitly chose for a small one. 0.04 is deliberately modest: at the existing DEFAULT_MAX_SIZE-class 1280x720@60, it computes to ~2.2Mbps (well under the 8Mbps default, so nothing changes there), while at dynamic_fit's ~3200x1800@60 ceiling it comes to ~13.8Mbps — close to the Settings panel's own "16 Mbps: 2K netlik için önerilen" guidance, and still under its 20Mbps maximum preset. |
| `OPENDEX_VIRTUAL_DISPLAY_DPI` | `int` | `420` | Fixed density for every virtual display. scrcpy's `new_display=WxH` (no /dpi) leaves density to an unspecified default — observed in practice to track the PHYSICAL device's own density (~440-460 for many phones). That silently caps dp-width (dpWidth = px / (dpi/160)) below Android's sw600dp tablet threshold no matter how many pixels are requested, since higher-density phones need MORE pixels just to stay phone-sized in dp. Pinning DPI ourselves makes the relation deterministic: more requested pixels -> proportionally more dp -> a big enough request genuinely crosses into tablet layout territory, matching how larger real devices differ from phones (more dp, not just more px). |
| `OPENDEX_UNFREEZE_GRACE_DELAY_S` | `float` | `0.2` | Grace period between stopping a window's OLD scrcpy server and spawning its replacement during freeze/unfreeze (minimize-restore, resize). Real-device testing (Xiaomi/HyperOS) showed the new app_process could get killed outright ("Aborted", not a Java exception) when spawned immediately after the previous one's teardown — releasing the prior virtual display/encoder is apparently not instantaneous even after our own stop() (sockets closed, local process reaped) returns. |

History kept in memory for the panel; samples also appended to logs/telemetry-YYYYMMDD.jsonl when TELEMETRY_RECORD. |

## Flex display

| Variable | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `OPENDEX_ENABLE_FLEX_DISPLAY` | `bool` | `true` | Resize a window's virtual display live (scrcpy v4 RESIZE_DISPLAY) instead of restarting its server, when phone and server support it. |
| `OPENDEX_MIN_API_FOR_FLEX_DISPLAY` | `int` | `29` | VirtualDisplay.resize() itself only needs API 28+; the binding constraint is already MIN_API_FOR_VIRTUAL_DISPLAY_LAUNCH=29 (no window exists below that). Kept as an INDEPENDENT constant (not reused directly) because real-device testing may need to raise it above 29 for a specific OEM without touching the unrelated virtual-display-launch gate. |

## Timeouts

| Variable | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `OPENDEX_FLEX_RESIZE_TIMEOUT_S` | `float` | `3.0` | Bound on waiting for the confirming session packet after RESIZE_DISPLAY (video socket). Not scrcpy's own server-side resize debounce — this is OUR ceiling on "how long do we wait before giving up and falling back to freeze/unfreeze for this one call". |
| `OPENDEX_RESIZE_MIN_INTERVAL_S` | `float` | `0.3` | Per-window resize safety belt (windows/resize_gate.py): at least this long between the END of one real resize and the start of the next; requests overtaken meanwhile are dropped (newest wins). Caps the phone at ~3 reconfigurations a second; a calm single resize waits 0. 0 = no wait, newest-wins still applies. |
| `OPENDEX_KEYFRAME_REQUEST_MIN_INTERVAL_S` | `float` | `1.5` | Keyframe on demand: least time between two requests for one window. The encoder's own keyframe interval is 60 s on the patched server (10 s upstream), so a decoder that lost its reference chain would otherwise show a frozen picture for up to that long. The interval keeps a stalled network from turning requests into a storm. |
| `OPENDEX_KEYFRAME_REQUEST_FALLBACK_S` | `float` | `1.0` | A server announcing "keyframe_request" is asked without an encoder restart; when no keyframe has arrived this long after (a codec that ignores the request), RESET_VIDEO — the restart — is sent after all. |
| `OPENDEX_NOTIFICATION_POLL_INTERVAL_S` | `float` | `10.0` | Phone notification safety net: logcat events already trigger a (debounced) `dumpsys notification` refresh; this periodic full dump only catches events logcat dropped. A full dump is large and every one is a new adb process sharing the video stream's single transport — it used to run every 2.5 s. |

## Density reconciliation

| Variable | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `OPENDEX_DENSITY_REFRESH_VERIFY_TIMEOUT_S` | `float` | `6.0` | An app process that lived through a display-density change is restarted (state preserving) once the change has settled. VERIFY_TIMEOUT: how long we wait for the process identity to change after asking Android to restart it. QUIET: a burst of density changes (dragging a DP slider) collapses into one restart after this much silence. MIN_GAP: never restart the same app twice within this window (restart-loop guard). |
| `OPENDEX_DENSITY_REFRESH_RELAUNCH_PROOF_S` | `float` | `2.5` | How long we wait for the system event log to show the in-place activity relaunch (`am update-appinfo`) before escalating to a process restart. |
| `OPENDEX_DENSITY_REFRESH_POLL_S` | `float` | `0.25` | poll interval while waiting for the app's process identity to change |
| `OPENDEX_DENSITY_REFRESH_QUIET_S` | `float` | `1.2` | a burst of density changes becomes ONE restart after this much silence |
| `OPENDEX_DENSITY_REFRESH_MIN_GAP_S` | `float` | `5.0` | never restart the same app twice within this many seconds |
| `OPENDEX_DENSITY_ADAPT_WAIT_S` | `float` | `1.5` | How long after the last density change the event log is watched for the app rebuilding ITSELF (Chrome recreates its activity on every density change; a move that changes the screen size makes Android relaunch many apps). Such an app is left alone — refreshing it again was the needless second refresh. |

## Encoder capacity stress test

| Variable | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `OPENDEX_STRESS_TEST_MAX_ATTEMPTS` | `int` | `16` | Empirically opens throwaway, app-less virtual displays until one fails, to measure the REAL concurrent-encoder ceiling instead of trusting the OEM's media_codecs.xml value (an upper-bound estimate, not a guarantee). comfortably above AOSP's documented sample max of 13 |
| `OPENDEX_STRESS_TEST_ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_S` | `float` | `6.0` | a full open+push+forward+spawn+handshake, not just a resize ack |
| `OPENDEX_STRESS_TEST_PROBE_DISPLAY_W` | `int` | `1280` | width of the throwaway probe displays |
| `OPENDEX_STRESS_TEST_PROBE_DISPLAY_H` | `int` | `720` | height of the probe displays |
| `OPENDEX_STRESS_TEST_PROBE_MAX_FPS` | `int` | `60` | Real-world operational defaults: tests true hardware VPU / bandwidth / pixel throughput ceiling under actual multi-window usage conditions (60 FPS, 8 Mbps, 720p+). |
| `OPENDEX_STRESS_TEST_PROBE_VIDEO_BIT_RATE` | `int` | `8000000` | bit/s of the probe streams |
